text:
andrew: Kicked off an active-sampling eval for neon-13b-int7 vs neon-13b-int8 using a 5k user-prompt sample. Goal: quantify unit-econ delta at slice level and decide product default.
claire: Nice. Is sampling stratified by intent? e.g., short answers vs long-context?
jai: Curious about throughput implications too — did you run on dedicated or hosted cluster?
andrew: Dedicated infra (staging dedicated pool). Yes — stratified into 4 slices: short_qa, multi_turn_chat, instruction, code_completion. Oversampled chat & code.
marta: Quick cost numbers from infra: int7 ~ $35 / 1M tokens, int8 ~ $80 / 1M tokens (includes KV cache overhead & extra memory pressure).
andrew: Primary quality metric is product-score (0-5) from side-by-side blind raters + automated proxies for regressions. Active sampling weights high-impact intents.
claire: Can you paste the sampling config?
andrew: ```json
{"sample_size":5000, "slices": {"short_qa": 0.25, "multi_chat": 0.4, "instruction": 0.2, "code": 0.15}, "oversample": "multi_chat" }
```
marta: Early results (rounded): int8 gains — multi_chat +5.3% absolute helpfulness, code +1.2%, instruction ~+0.6%, short_qa ~0.0%.
jai: Nice. What's the token profile per slice? Need to convert to per-interaction cost delta.
andrew: Per-slice median tokens per interaction (k tokens): short_qa 15k, multi_chat 200k, instruction 40k, code 150k. Int8-int7 cost delta ~ $45 / 1M tokens => extra cost per interaction approx: short_qa $0.000675, multi_chat $0.009, instruction $0.0018, code $0.00675. Weighted by slice weights (and oversample): blended extra cost per interaction ~ $0.0036.
claire: Product-side extrapolation: multi_chat +5% helpfulness roughly maps to +0.2% retention in our cohort experiments, that maps to ~ $0.05 ARPU uplift per MAU over 30d (very noisy estimate).
marta: Let's convert to cost-per-helpful-unit (CPHU). If 1 helpful-unit == 1% helpfulness increase across N interactions, simpler to reason per-slice.
andrew: Draft scorecard (rounded):
- short_qa: CPHU = $0.02
- multi_chat: CPHU = $0.30
- instruction: CPHU = $0.05
- code: CPHU = $0.18
Overall blended CPHU = $0.12
(These combine token-cost delta, slice frequency, and observed quality delta -> see spreadsheet in artifacts.)
jai: Operational rec: keep neon-13b-int7 as platform default to control unit costs. Enable neon-13b-int8 for: paid tier chat routes, code-completion flagged customers, and experimental GTN cohorts. Use hybrid routing where int8 only for the last-turn scoring or high-latency-tolerant calls.
claire: :thumbsup: Also recommend a 2-week canary with live active-sampling and cost alerts (sliding window on $/min and QPS).
andrew: Agreed — I'll draft GTN brief + rollout flags. Will include playbook for fallback to int7 when avg latency > target or cost burn spikes.
deploy-bot: artifact neon-active-sample-v1 uploaded -> s3://redwood-evals/neon/1722223333.tar.gz (checksums: sha256:abcd1234)
marta: Thanks — will sync with product/pricing tomorrow and add a short summary for sales enablement.
claire: Ping me once the canary config is live, I can wire the alerting dashboard.
andrew: Will follow up with the spreadsheet and traffic-split config. Thanks everyone.
